plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial with large, fragrant, bowl-shaped to fully double flowers atop sturdy stems with deeply lobed glossy green foliage. Long-lived and often thriving for decades in the same spot.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (May to early June) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to China, Mongolia and Siberia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Peonies have been cultivated in China for over 2,000 years, and some plants can live and bloom for more than 100 years. Ants visiting the buds feed on nectar and do not need to be removed for the flowers to open.

plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub producing dense conical clusters of intensely fragrant, small tubular flowers with four-lobed petals. It is a beloved garden shrub in cool temperate regions and peaks in mid-May in many areas.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (late April to late May)
plants.location: Native to the Balkan Peninsula in southeastern Europe; cultivated throughout temperate North America, Europe and northern Asia
plants.funFact: Lilac needs a cold winter dormancy to bloom well, so it struggles in tropical climates. It is the state flower of New Hampshire because it symbolizes the hardy character of its people.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, semi-deciduous tree with fern-like foliage that bursts into a canopy of trumpet-shaped violet-blue flowers, carpeting the ground beneath it. In the Northern Hemisphere subtropics it begins blooming in late spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June) in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics; October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in Mediterranean climates, California, Florida, Mexico, South Africa and Australia
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, so many jacarandas line the streets that the city is nicknamed the Jacaranda City, and in parts of Mexico the blooms are celebrated as a sign of spring.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and delicate, slightly fragrant flowers that open in cool weather. In the Southern Hemisphere, it begins flowering as autumn arrives and the days cool.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (April to July) in the Southern Hemisphere; autumn in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely grown in Australia, New Zealand, southern Africa, and the southern United States
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is closely related to Camellia sinensis, the tea plant, and its seeds are pressed to produce a culinary and cosmetic oil used in Japan.
